s: Agîva is a existent entity
q: Do not maintain that Gîva and Agîva do not exist, but that they exist.

q: Do not maintain that Dharma and Adharma do not exist, but that they exist.

s: bondage is a existent state
q: Do not maintain that bondage and liberation do not exist, but that they exist.

s: Liberation is a existent state
q: Do not maintain that bondage and liberation do not exist, but that they exist.

s: clever monk practises vow of chastity
q: A very clever (monk) who practises the vow of chastity, should not adopt the following (heretical) doctrines, nor behave badly in this religion.

s: Âsrava is a existent condition
q: Do not maintain that Âsrava and the stoppage of Âsrava do not exist, but that they exist.

s: stoppage of Âsrava is a existent condition
q: Do not maintain that Âsrava and the stoppage of Âsrava do not exist, but that they exist.

q: Do not maintain that the experiencing of the effect, and the annihilation of Karman do not exist, but that they exist.

s: mental, verbal, and bodily activity is a existent condition
q: Do not maintain that activity and non-activity do not exist, but that they exist.

s: clever monk improves chances for final liberation (instead of focusing on receiving alms)
q: A wise monk should not say: we get alms (from this householder) or we do not; but he should improve his chances for final liberation.

s: fourfold Circle of Births is a existent cycle (fourfold)
q: Do not maintain that the fourfold Circle of Births does not exist, but that it exists.

s: gods exist in the world
q: Do not maintain that there are no gods and goddesses, but that there are.

s: perfection is a existent state
q: Do not maintain that there is no such thing as perfection and non-perfection, but that there is such a thing.

s: clever monk conforms to opinions taught by the Ginas
q: A monk should conform himself to these opinions taught by the Ginas, and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: wrongly instructed Sramanas do not comprehend bondage (through Karman)
q: The wrongly instructed Sramanas do not comprehend the (soul's) bondage (through Karman).

s: Ginas teach opinions
q: A monk should conform himself to these opinions taught by the Ginas, and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: final beatitude is a ultimate destination (for a wandering monk)
q: A monk should conform himself to these opinions taught by the Ginas, and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: clever monk wanders until final beatitude
q: A monk should conform himself to these opinions taught by the Ginas, and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: beings know and teach truth
q: One should not say: that there will be an end of beings who (know and) teach the truth;

s: truth is inaccessible through alternatives (heretical alternatives)
q: From these alternatives you cannot arrive at truth; from these alternatives you are, certainly, led to error.

s: error results from alternatives (heretical alternatives)
q: From these alternatives you cannot arrive at truth; from these alternatives you are, certainly, led to error.

s: Sramanas teach the five small vows
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: Sramanas avoid Karman (in the blessed life of Sramanas)
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: Sramanas are not householders (when they use cold water, eat seeds, or have intercourse with women)
q: Know this: those who use cold water, eat seeds, accept things especially prepared for them, and have intercourse with women, are (no better than) householders, but they are no Sramanas.

s: monks are reborn again and again (when they eat seeds and use cold water)
q: Monks who eat seeds and use cold water, who beg alms as a means of living, will, though they leave their relations, be born again and again, and will not put an end to mundane existence.

s: monks do not end fourfold Circle of Births (when they eat seeds and use cold water)
q: Monks who eat seeds and use cold water, who beg alms as a means of living, will, though they leave their relations, be born again and again, and will not put an end to mundane existence.

s: householders are sramanas Sramanas (if those who eat seeds, use cold water, and have intercourse with women are admitted to be Sramanas)
q: If those who eat seeds, use (cold) water, and have intercourse with women, are admitted to be Sramanas, then householders too are Sramanas; for they do the same things.

s: philosophers praise their own doctrines
q: Every philosopher praises his own doctrines and makes them known.

s: philosophers make known doctrines (their own)
q: Every philosopher praises his own doctrines and makes them known.

s: Mahâvîra is a Sramana (also called Gñâtriputra)
q: As a merchant desirous of gain (shows) his wares and attracts a crowd to do business, in a similar way (acts) the Sramana Gñâtriputra.

s: right conduct avoids sin (through abstention from wicked deeds)
q: A man who knows the nature of movable and immovable living beings, above, below, and on earth, who is afraid of injuring them and abstains from wicked deeds, may speak and act (in accordance with our Law); he will not be guilty of any (sin).

s: living beings are movable and immovable movable and immovable (above, below, and on earth)
q: A man who knows the nature of movable and immovable living beings, above, below, and on earth, who is afraid of injuring them and abstains from wicked deeds, may speak and act (in accordance with our Law); he will not be guilty of any (sin).

s: the Law enjoins compassion
q: He who despises the Law that enjoins compassion, and praises the Law that permits slaughter, and who feeds but a single unprincipled man, even if he be a king, will go to darkness, and not to the gods.

s: the Law permits slaughter (according to the condemned doctrine)
q: He who despises the Law that enjoins compassion, and praises the Law that permits slaughter, and who feeds but a single unprincipled man, even if he be a king, will go to darkness, and not to the gods.

s: compassion is enjoined by the Law
q: He who despises the Law that enjoins compassion, and praises the Law that permits slaughter, and who feeds but a single unprincipled man, even if he be a king, will go to darkness, and not to the gods.

s: Karman is avoided by Sramanas (in the blessed life of Sramanas)
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: Môksha is the gain Sramanas (desired by a Sramana)
q: Herein is contained the vow (leading to) Brahman (i.e. Môksha); this is the gain which a Sramana is desirous of.

s: fourfold Circle of Births is endless endless (for those bound by slaughter and acquisition of property)
q: They do not abstain from slaughter and the acquirement of property, they are in bondage and full of wickedness; and their gain of which you spoke,. will be the endless Circle of Births and pains manifold.

s: fourfold Circle of Births contains pains manifold (as an endless cycle)
q: They do not abstain from slaughter and the acquirement of property, they are in bondage and full of wickedness; and their gain of which you spoke,. will be the endless Circle of Births and pains manifold.

s: Mahâvîra teaches the Law (to many monks)
q: At first he wandered about as a single monk; but now he has surrounded himself by many monks, and teaches every one of them the Law at length.

s: Kêvala knowledge knows all things (when full)
q: Those who know all things by the full Kêvala knowledge, and who practising meditation teach the whole Law, are themselves saved and save others.

s: Kêvala knowledge saves those who possess it (with meditation and teaching of the whole Law)
q: Those who know all things by the full Kêvala knowledge, and who practising meditation teach the whole Law, are themselves saved and save others.

s: sin is incurred by slaughter (even when only one animal is killed annually)
q: If every year you kill but one animal without abstaining from sin, though you are not guilty of the slaughter of other creatures, there is little difference between you and a householder.

s: slaughter causes perdition (even when only one animal is killed annually)
q: If a man kills every year but one animal, and lives (in other respects) as a Sramana, he is unworthy, and works his perdition.

s: slaughter is caused by a fattened sheep (when killed and prepared as food for a particular person)
q: They kill a fattened sheep, and prepare food for the sake of a particular person; they season the meat with salt and oil, and dress it with pepper.

s: Mahâvîra is single and alone single and alone (though surrounded by many followers)
q: His past, present, and future lives agree with each other; for he is really always single and alone (though he be now surrounded by many followers).

s: householders use cold water
q: If those who eat seeds, use (cold) water, and have intercourse with women, are admitted to be Sramanas, then householders too are Sramanas; for they do the same things.

s: householders eat seeds
q: If those who eat seeds, use (cold) water, and have intercourse with women, are admitted to be Sramanas, then householders too are Sramanas; for they do the same things.

s: householders have intercourse with women
q: If those who eat seeds, use (cold) water, and have intercourse with women, are admitted to be Sramanas, then householders too are Sramanas; for they do the same things.

s: the great vows are taught by Sramanas
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: the five small vows are taught by Sramanas
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: Mahâvîra avoids wrong opinions
q: (Mahâvîra) acquires no new (Karman), he annihilates the old, avoiding wrong opinions;

s: Mahâvîra acquires no new Karman
q: (Mahâvîra) acquires no new (Karman), he annihilates the old, avoiding wrong opinions;

s: Mahâvîra annihilates old Karman
q: (Mahâvîra) acquires no new (Karman), he annihilates the old, avoiding wrong opinions;

s: Sramanas teach the great vows
q: He who (teaches) the great vows (of monks) and the five small vows (of the laity), the five Âsravas and the stoppage of the Âsravas, and control, who avoids Karman in this blessed life of Sramanas, him I call a Sramana.

s: Gautama stay in the garden (as the Venerable Gautama)
q: And there in some house the Venerable Gautama was staying. The venerable (man) was in the garden

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla is a Nirgrantha Sramanas (and follower of Pârsva)
q: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla, a Nirgrantha and follower of Pârsva, of the Mêdârya Gôtra

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla follows Pârsva (as a Nirgrantha)
q: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla, a Nirgrantha and follower of Pârsva, of the Mêdârya Gôtra

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla belongs to Mêdârya Gôtra
q: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla, a Nirgrantha and follower of Pârsva, of the Mêdârya Gôtra

s: Kumâraputras is a Nirgrantha Sramanas (professing Gautama's creed)
q: there are Nirgrantha Sramanas, called Kumâraputras, who profess your creed

s: Nirgrantha Sramanas make void renunciation of injury to living beings (when they permit injury to some classes of beings)
q: They make void all vows undertaken for sparing particular living beings.

s: living beings belong to fourfold Circle of Births
q: Beings belong to the Circle of Births

s: movable beings are subject to Karman (through the taking effect of Karman relating to movable beings)
q: Movable beings are called so, when they get this character through the taking effect of the Karman relating to movable beings.

s: immovable living beings are subject to Karman (through the taking effect of Karman relating to immovable beings)
q: Immovable beings are called so, when they get this character through the taking effect of the Karman relating to immovable beings.

s: movable beings become immovable living beings (after the duration of life as movable beings ends)
q: But when their duration of life as movable beings comes to its close, the (soul), embodied in a movable being, leaves its life as such and becomes embodied in an immovable being.

s: immovable living beings take new form of existence new form of existence (after the duration of life as an immovable being ends)
q: But when their duration of life as an immovable being comes to its close, the (soul), embodied in an immovable being, leaves its life as such and takes again a new form of existence

s: movable beings are sinful to kill sin (when they are born in bodies of movable beings)
q: when they are born in bodies of movable beings, it is a sin to kill them.

s: immovable living beings not be sinful to kill them (when they are born in bodies of immovable beings)
q: When they are born in bodies of immovable beings, it is no sin to kill them.

s: Gautama rejects Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla (his interpretation of renunciation)
q: O long-lived Udaka, we certainly do not approve of it.

s: Gautama teaches renunciation of injury to living beings (as applying to all kinds of living beings)
q: There are always a great many animate beings, (the slaughter of) which a follower of the Sramanas must renounce, there are none, (the slaughter of) which he need not renounce.

s: renunciation of injury to living beings is good good renunciation (when injury to the large class of movable beings is abandoned)
q: If he ceases, or has done with, or has given up (injuring) the large class of movable beings, his renunciation is good.

s: Nâlandâ is a suburb (outside Râgagriha in a north-eastern direction)
q: Outside of Râgagriha, in a north-eastern direction, there was the suburb Nâlandâ

s: Law is instructed to householders or sons of householders (when they come for instruction)
q: O long-lived Nirgranthas, (suppose) there be householders or sons of householders, born in respectable families, who come to you for instruction in the Law. Ought they to be instructed in the Law?" 'Yes, they should

s: the creed which enjoins four vows is a creed
q: I desire, Reverend Sir, in your presence to pass from the creed which enjoins four vows

s: the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana is a creed
q: to the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana.

s: Pratikramana is enjoined by the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana
q: the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana

s: death and rebirth is governed by Karman (in the next existence)
q: Then they die; in their next existence they experience their Karman, and receive an evil lot.

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla respects Gautama (after understanding Gautama's teaching)
q: But now, Reverend Sir, as I do know, &c., these words which I have perceived, heard, &c., I believe, accept, and approve of their meaning. It is just as you say!'

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla passes from the creed which enjoins four vows (in Gautama's presence)
q: I desire, Reverend Sir, in your presence to pass from the creed which enjoins four vows

s: Nâlandâ contains many hundreds of buildings
q: it contained many hundreds of buildings, &c.

s: Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla passes to the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana (in the presence of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra)
q: Then, in the presence of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra, Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla, passed from the creed which enjoins four vows, to the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana.

s: Mahâvîra be present at Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla
q: Then, in the presence of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra, Udaka, the son of Pêdhâla, passed from the creed which enjoins four vows, to the creed which enjoins the five great vows and the Pratikramana.

s: householder Lêpa follows followers of the Sramanas (as a householder)
q: This householder Lêpa, a follower of the Sramanas

s: householder Lêpa comprehends living beings (and things without life)
q: This householder Lêpa, a follower of the Sramanas, comprehended (the doctrine of) living beings and things without life

s: karman is owned by men (as acknowledged in judgments such as 'I did it')
q: He believes in soul, believes in the world, believes in reward, believes in action (acknowledged to be our own doing in such judgments as these): 'I did it;' 'I shall cause another to do it;' 'I shall allow another to do it.'

s: sin has causes karman (in the world)
q: In the world, these are all the causes of sin, which must be comprehended and renounced.

s: sin causes samsâra (when not comprehended and renounced)
q: A man that does not comprehend and renounce the causes of sin, descends in a cardinal or intermediate direction, wanders to all cardinal or intermediate directions, is born again and again in manifold births

s: sin causes pain (when not comprehended and renounced)
q: A man that does not comprehend and renounce the causes of sin, descends in a cardinal or intermediate direction, wanders to all cardinal or intermediate directions, is born again and again in manifold births, experiences all painful feelings.

s: sin is comprehended and renounced by men (as taught by the Revered One)
q: He who, in the world, comprehends and renounces these causes of sin, is called a reward-knowing sage (muni).

s: men are afflicted by pain (in the living world)
q: The (living) world is afflicted, miserable, difficult to instruct, and without discrimination.

s: living beings are individually embodied earth-bodies
q: See! there are beings individually embodied (in earth; not one all-soul).

s: living beings experience pain (individually, across the forms of life)
q: all beings, those with two, three, four senses, plants, those with five senses, and the rest of creation, (experience) individually pleasure or displeasure, pain, great terror, and unhappiness.

s: houselessness is called houseless (acts rightly, does pious work, and practises no deceit)
q: He who acts rightly, who does pious work, who practises no deceit, is called houseless.

s: Akaranga Sutra (Âkârâṅga Sûtra) contains First Book
q: First Book.

s: earth-bodies are living living beings (individually embodied)
q: See! there are beings individually embodied (in earth; not one all-soul).

s: water-bodies are living living beings (many lives inhabit water)
q: There are beings living in water, many lives; of a truth, to the monks water has been declared to be living matter.

s: water-bodies are living matter (according to the monks)
q: There are beings living in water, many lives; of a truth, to the monks water has been declared to be living matter.

s: fire-bodies is destroyed by bad and injurious doings
q: See! there are men who control themselves; others pretend only to be houseless; for one destroys this (fire-body) by bad and injurious doings, and many other beings, besides, which he hurts by means of fire

s: plants are like men (in birth, growth, illness, nourishment, decay, change and impermanence)
q: As the nature of this (i.e. men) is to be born and to grow old, so is the nature of that (i.e. plants) to be born and to grow old; as this has reason, so that has reason; as this falls sick when cut, so that falls sick when cut; as this needs food, so that needs food; as this will decay, so that will decay; as this is not eternal, so that is not eternal; as this takes increment, so that takes increment; as this is changing, so that is changing.

s: animals is destroyed by bad and injurious doings
q: See! there are men who control themselves; others pretend only to be houseless, for one destroys this (body of an animal) by bad and injurious doings, and many other beings, besides, which he hurts by means of animals

s: wind-bodies is destroyed by bad and injurious doings
q: See! there are men who control themselves; others pretend only to be houseless, for one destroys this (wind-body) by bad and injurious doings, and many other beings, besides, which he hurts by means of wind

s: aggregate of six kinds of lives is addressed as aggregate of six (kinds of) lives (a wise man should not act sinfully towards it)
q: Knowing them, a wise man should not act sinfully towards the aggregate of six (kinds of) lives

s: religious faith is informed from the Revered One or the monks (when understood or heard)
q: About this he is informed when he has understood or heard, either from the Revered One or from the monks, the faith to be coveted.

s: final liberation is sought by men (alongside birth and death)
q: for the sake of birth, death, and final liberation, for the removal of pain

s: First Book contains Knowledge of the Weapon
q: First Lecture, Called Knowledge of the Weapon.

s: men are called reward-knowing sages (when they know and renounce causes of sin)
q: He who knows these causes of sin relating to animals, is called a reward-knowing sage. Thus I say. (6)

s: Knowledge of the Weapon contains First Lesson
q: First Lesson.

s: Knowledge of the Weapon contains Seventh Lesson
q: Seventh Lesson.

s: Sudharman heard from Mahâvîra (as a discourse)
q: I (Sudharman) have heard the following discourse from the venerable (Mahâvîra): (1)

s: Self is born again again and again (according to the teaching)
q: Similarly, some know that their soul is born again and again

s: world is believed in by men
q: He believes in soul, believes in the world, believes in reward, believes in action

s: Second Lecture, Called Conquest of the World is a lecture
q: Second Lecture, Called Conquest of the World.

s: hero is not polluted by violence (the sin of killing)
q: the hero is not polluted by the sin of killing.

s: houseless is a desireless person (who has given up the world and ceased to act)
q: Desireless, giving up the world, and ceasing to act, he knows, and sees, and has no wishes because of his discernment; he is called houseless.

s: sage is a person who has passed over samsara (and ceased from all activity)
q: Such a man is said to have crossed the flood (of life), to be a sage, to have passed over (the samsâra), to be liberated, to have ceased (from all activity).

s: fool is a worldly-minded person (who longs for life)
q: And a fool who longs for life, and worldly-minded, laments that (for these worldly goods) penance, self-restraint, and control do not avail, will ignorantly come to grief.

s: fool comes to grief through worldly attachment (ignorantly)
q: Thus a fool doing cruel deeds which benefit another, will ignorantly come thereby to grief.

s: living beings are fond of life (and dislike pain and destruction)
q: All beings are fond of life, like pleasure, hate pain, shun destruction, like life, long to live.

s: mortal people are attached to wealth and treasures (including clothes, jewels, gold, and women)
q: Having acquired dyed and coloured (clothes), jewels, earrings, gold, and women, they become attached to these things.

s: women cause pain (through worldly delusion)
q: The world is greatly troubled by women.

s: women lead to death (as objects called vessels of happiness)
q: The world is greatly troubled by women. They (viz. men) forsooth say, 'These are the vessels (of happiness).' But this leads them to pain, to delusion, to death, to hell, to birth as hell-beings or brute beasts.

s: self-control causes hardships (he is not vexed by them)
q: He is called a hero who is not vexed by (the hardships caused) by control.

s: passions is subdued by desirelessness
q: Subduing desire by desirelessness, he does not enjoy the pleasures that offer themselves.

s: sensual enjoyment causes pain (when desired worldly goods are lost)
q: Pleasures are difficult to reject, life is difficult to prolong. That man, certainly, who loves pleasures, is afflicted (by their loss), is sorry in his heart, leaves his usual ways, is troubled, suffers pain.

s: sensual enjoyment causes delusion (through worldly attachment)
q: But this leads them to pain, to delusion, to death, to hell, to birth as hell-beings or brute beasts.

s: wealth and treasures are divided by inheritance division (among heirs)
q: Then at another time, his heirs divide it,

s: wealth and treasures are lost through theft (by those without a living)
q: or those who are without a living steal it,

s: wealth and treasures are destroyed by house conflagration (when the house burns)
q: or it is consumed by the conflagration of the house.

s: world is a realm of samsara (in which desire causes repeated birth and death)
q: He who knows the relation (of human affairs, viz.) that he who desires for the world is always turned round (in the samsâra),

s: monk recognises proper moment (for entering religious life)
q: Knowing pain and pleasure in all their variety, and seeing his life not yet decline, a wise man should know that to be the proper moment (for entering a religious life);

s: violence is done by mortal people (deliberately, out of fear, or for hoped-for expiation)
q: Thus violence is done by these various acts, deliberately, out of fear, because they think 'it is for the expiation of sins,' or for some other hope.

s: non-killing is a true knowledge (joined with renunciation)
q: Observing (the pain of mundane existence, one should) not (act) with violence. This is called the true knowledge (and renunciation).

s: birth and death cause pain (in the whirl of existence)
q: Not enlightened (about the cause of these ills) he is afflicted (by them), always turns round (in the whirl of) birth and death.

s: samsâra is a whirl of birth and death (from which the wise seek liberation)
q: who desires for the world is always turned round (in the samsâra)

s: opposite shore is reached by those freed from attachment (to the world and its pleasures)
q: Those who are freed (from attachment to the world and its pleasures), reach the opposite shore.

s: the body is loathsome interior and exterior (both inwardly and outwardly)
q: As the interior (of the body is loathsome), so is the exterior; as the exterior, so is the interior.

s: the body sustains pain (when its painful nature is perceived)
q: but when he perceives that this body sustains pains, he cries in his ignorance.

s: monk should remove aversion (to control)
q: A wise man should remove any aversion (to control); he will be liberated in the proper time.

s: monk should not commit violence (by such acts)
q: Knowing this, a wise man should neither himself commit violence by such acts, nor order others to commit violence by such acts, nor consent to the violence done by somebody else.

s: monk should enter law (before old age begins)
q: Knowing birth and death, one should firmly walk the path (i.e. right conduct), (and not wait for old age to commence a religious life),

s: hero is a person who is not vexed by hardships (caused by control)
q: He is called a hero who is not vexed by (the hardships caused) by control.

s: hero liberates living beings (those who are fettered)
q: is called among mortals a hero, who liberates those who are fettered.

s: Third Lecture, Called Hot and Cold is a lecture
q: Third Lecture, Called Hot and Cold.

s: hero guards self (carefully abstaining from pleasures and ceasing from bad works)
q: Carefully abstaining from pleasures and ceasing from bad works he is a hero, guarding himself, who is grounded in knowledge.

s: hero is grounded in knowledge
q: Carefully abstaining from pleasures and ceasing from bad works he is a hero, guarding himself, who is grounded in knowledge.

s: hero should conquer wrath and pride
q: And the hero should conquer wrath and pride, Look at the great hell (as the place) for greed.

s: men is subject to old age (when always benighted)
q: But a man always benighted, subject to old age and death, does not know the law.

s: men is subject to death (when always benighted)
q: But a man always benighted, subject to old age and death, does not know the law.

s: men should lead religious life (after seeing living beings suffering)
q: Seeing living beings suffering, earnestly enter a religious life.

s: living beings arise from karman (their condition)
q: The condition of living beings arises from karman.

s: living beings suffer misery (in the world)
q: Waking and free from hostility, a wise man, thou liberatest (thyself and others) from the miseries.

s: Mâra is avoided by men (through upright conduct and disregard of sensual objects)
q: Knowing the misery that results from action, The deluded and careless one returns to life; Disregarding sounds and colours, upright, Avoiding Mâra one is liberated from death.

s: world has misery (as a consequence of action)
q: Knowing the misery that results from action

s: monk is a one who knows the law (when self-possessed, wise, just, chaste, and understanding the world)
q: he is to be called a sage, one who knows the law, and righteous.

s: world has connection (with birth and sensation through love and hate)
q: He knows the connection of the whirl (of births) and the current (of sensation with love and hate).

s: law is known by monk
q: he is to be called a sage, one who knows the law, and righteous.

s: karman causes birth (through attachment to pleasures)
q: Desirous of pleasures they heap up karman, Influenced by it they are born again.

s: karman has root in violence (especially killing)
q: Examining karman and the root of karman, viz. killing

s: violence is done for special objects
q: He who knows the violence done for the sake of special objects, knows what is free from violence

s: nonviolence is known by he who knows what is free from violence (he knows the violence done for special objects)
q: he who knows what is free from violence, knows the violence done for special objects.

s: monk possesses sensual perceptions (correctly)
q: He who correctly possesses these (sensual perceptions), viz. sounds, and colours, and smells, and tastes, and touches (1), who self-possessed, wise, just, chaste, with right comprehension understands the world, he is to be called a sage, one who knows the law, and righteous.

s: highest good is known by most learned (with right intuition)
q: Thence the most learned, knowing (what is called) the highest good, He who has right intuition, commits no sin.

s: highest good is known by monk (as the goal of circumspect religious life)
q: he is a sage who sees the danger, knowing the highest good in this world, leading a circumspect life

s: truth destroys karman (when delighted in by a wise man)
q: Delighting in it, a wise man destroys all karman.

s: Brahman follows Gainas (their unrivalled control)
q: the Brahman follows the unrivalled (control of the Gainas).

s: monk knows law (with right comprehension)
q: he is to be called a sage, one who knows the law, and righteous.

s: Tîrthakaras command religious conduct (according to their commandment)
q: Faithful according to the commandment (of the Tîrthakaras), wise, and understanding the world according to the commandment--such a man is without danger from anywhere.

s: mortal people are small ones (in contrast with gods)
q: being with a great one (i.e. a god) or the small ones (men)

s: birth leads to death (through the worldly chain)
q: he who knows conception, knows birth; he who knows birth, knows death

s: death leads to hell (in the chain of worldly existence)
q: he who knows death, knows hell; he who knows hell, knows animal existence

s: animal existence leads to pain (in the chain of worldly existence)
q: he who knows hell, knows animal existence; he who knows animal existence, knows pain.

s: passions include wrath
q: Therefore, a wise man should avoid wrath, pride, deceit, greed, love, hate, delusion, conception, birth, death, hell, animal existence, and pain.

s: passions include pride
q: Therefore, a wise man should avoid wrath, pride, deceit, greed, love, hate, delusion, conception, birth, death, hell, animal existence, and pain.

s: monk knows world (with right comprehension)
q: who self-possessed, wise, just, chaste, with right comprehension understands the world

s: passions include deceit
q: Therefore, a wise man should avoid wrath, pride, deceit, greed, love, hate, delusion, conception, birth, death, hell, animal existence, and pain.

s: passions include greed
q: Therefore, a wise man should avoid wrath, pride, deceit, greed, love, hate, delusion, conception, birth, death, hell, animal existence, and pain.

s: samsâra is ended by Seer (when acts and worldly existence have ended)
q: This is the doctrine of the Seer who does not injure living beings and has put an end (to acts and to samsâra).

s: doctrine of the Seer teaches nonviolence (the Seer does not injure living beings)
q: This is the doctrine of the Seer, who does not injure living beings and has put an end (to acts and to samsâra).

s: great journey is taken by hero (after rejecting connection with the world)
q: Knowing the misery of the world' rejecting the connection with the world, 'the heroes go on the great journey,' they rise gradually

s: monk is righteous righteous
q: he is to be called a sage, one who knows the law, and righteous.

s: Nirgrantha is equanimous toward heat and cold (not minding them)
q: Not minding heat and cold, equanimous against pleasure and pain, the Nirgrantha does not feel the austerity of penance.

s: Nirgrantha is equanimous toward pleasure and pain
q: Not minding heat and cold, equanimous against pleasure and pain, the Nirgrantha does not feel the austerity of penance.

s: Nirgrantha does not feel austerity of penance
q: Not minding heat and cold, equanimous against pleasure and pain, the Nirgrantha does not feel the austerity of penance.

s: Fourth Lecture, Called Righteousness is a lecture
q: Fourth Lecture, Called Righteousness.

s: âsravas are as many as parisravas
q: There are as many âsravas as there are parisravas

s: anâsravas are as many as aparisravas
q: There are as many anâsravas as there are aparisravas

s: samsâra is a cycle of rebirth
q: who still belong to the samsâra, who are awakened, and have reached discrimination.

s: death is inescapable nothing secure (for the afflicted and careless)
q: There is nothing secure from the mouth of death.

s: pain is unpleasant all sorts of living beings (disagreeable and greatly feared)
q: For all sorts of living beings pain is unpleasant, disagreeable. and greatly feared.

s: Brâhmanas raise discussion (in this world)
q: Many and several in this world, Brâhmanas or Sramanas, raise this discussion

s: Sramanas raise discussion (in this world)
q: Many and several in this world, Brâhmanas or Sramanas, raise this discussion

s: the professors are conversant with pain (all)
q: All the professors, conversant with pain, preach renunciation.

s: the professors preach renunciation (all)
q: All the professors, conversant with pain, preach renunciation.

s: the teachers teach nonviolence (as their doctrine)
q: But we say thus, speak thus, declare thus, explain thus: All sorts of living beings should not be slain, nor treated with violence, nor abused, nor tormented, nor driven away. Know about this, there is no wrong in it. This is the doctrine of the teachers.

s: renunciation is preached by the professors (by those conversant with pain)
q: All the professors, conversant with pain, preach renunciation.

s: the body should be subdued self-discipline (by the wise and unattached)
q: Thus thoroughly knowing karman, observing the commandment, wise, unattached (to the world), recognising thy Self as one, subdue the body, chastise thyself, weaken thyself

s: hero are careful restraint (always)
q: Therefore a hero is careful, a person of pith, guarded, endowed (with knowledge, &c.), and always restrained.

s: hero pursue final liberation (on a difficult road)
q: Difficult to go is the road of the heroes, who go whence there is no return (final liberation).

s: living beings should not be slain nonviolence
q: all breathing, existing, living, sentient creatures should not be slain, nor treated with violence, nor abused, nor tormented, nor driven away.

s: the aggregate is shaken off by hero (through chastity)
q: That man is called a worthy one, a hero, one to be followed, who living in chastity [guarding his eyes] shakes off the aggregate.

s: freedom from acts is known by he who among mortals
q: he who among mortals knows freedom from acts

s: the Seer has no worldly weakness (none exists)
q: Is there any worldly weakness in the Seer? There exists none, there is none. Thus I say.

s: living beings should not be treated with violence nonviolence
q: all breathing, existing, living, sentient creatures should not be slain, nor treated with violence, nor abused, nor tormented, nor driven away.

s: law is a law (pure, unchangeable, eternal)
q: This is the pure, unchangeable, eternal law, which the clever ones, who understand the world, have declared

s: law applies to world (among all kinds of people)
q: among the zealous and the not zealous, among the faithful and the not faithful, among the not cruel and the cruel, among those who have worldly weakness and those who have not, among those who like social bonds and those who do not: 'that is the truth, that is so, that is proclaimed in this (creed).'

s: world contains worldly weakness (in some persons)
q: among those who have worldly weakness and those who have not

s: world contains worldly pleasures (as objects of attachment)
q: Those who acquiesce and indulge (in worldly pleasures), are born again and again.

s: Fifth Lecture, called Essence of the World is a Lecture
q: Fifth Lecture, Called Essence of the World.

s: heretics lead religious life (as hermits)
q: Many (heretics) lead the life of a hermit (in order to avoid worldly sorrows and pains).

s: fool has wrath (much)
q: Such a man has much wrath, much pride, much conceit, much greed;

s: fool has greed (much)
q: Such a man has much wrath, much pride, much conceit, much greed;

s: fool is influenced by ignorance and carelessness
q: Through the influence of ignorance and carelessness the fool never knows the law.

s: fool does not know law (through ignorance and carelessness)
q: Through the influence of ignorance and carelessness the fool never knows the law.

s: samsâra is a whirlpool (of births)
q: they turn round and round in the whirlpool (of births).

s: injurious deeds are not lived by many (against the world and these living beings)
q: Many do not live by injurious deeds against the world, they do not live by injurious deeds against these (living beings). Ceasing from them, making an end of them, he perceives: this is a favourable opportunity;

s: monk is a true monk (when neither killing nor lying and bearing unpleasant feelings)
q: Neither killing nor lying, he should (patiently) bear (all unpleasant) feelings when affected by them. That man is called a true monk.

s: world contains six classes of living beings (as objects of cruel thoughts)
q: Many entertain cruel thoughts against the world with a motive or without one; they entertain cruel thoughts against these (six classes of living beings).

s: pleasure and pain is known by he (in their various forms)
q: When he has become zealous for the law, he should never be careless, knowing pain and pleasure in their various forms.

s: the body is fragile (decaying, unstable, transient, uneternal, increasing and decreasing, and changeable)
q: (The body) is of a fragile, decaying nature, (it is) unstable, transient, uneternal, increasing and decreasing, of a changeable nature.

s: worldly attachments include living beings (sentient or nonsentient)
q: Many are attached to something in the world--be it little or much, small or great, sentient or nonsentient--they are attached to it (here) amongst these (householders).

s: sagedom is righteousness (what is acknowledged as righteousness)
q: What you acknowledge as righteousness, that you acknowledge as sagedom (mauna); what you acknowledge as sagedom, that you acknowledge as righteousness.

s: houseless suffers pain (with patience for a long time)
q: He who has ceased (to have worldly attachments), the houseless, suffers with patience a long time.

s: religious life is led by careful (in contrast to the careless)
q: The careless stand outside, the careful lead a religious life.

s: sensual enjoyment are dear to fool
q: To him pleasures are dear.

s: religion of the Gainas declares colour (as a cause of the fool's fall)
q: In this (religion of the Gainas the cause of the fool's fall) has been declared (to depend) on colour and killing.

s: wisdom is praised by clever ones (as discernment)
q: For the clever ones have praised the discernment of wisdom;

s: sage does not kill living beings (knowing the nature of acts)
q: 'Knowing thus (the nature of) acts in all regards, he does not kill,' he controls himself, he is not overbearing.

s: Mahavîra is clever one the clever one
q: That is the doctrine of the clever one (Mahavîra).

s: âkârya is guide and adviser (for the monk)
q: Adopting the (âkârya's) views, imitating his indifference (for the outer world), making him the guide and adviser (in all one's matters),

s: women are greatest temptation (in this world)
q: The greatest temptation in this world are women.

s: lake contains water-bodies (full and in an even plain)
q: Thus I say: a lake is full of water, it is in an even plain, it is free from dust, it harbours (many fish).

s: fool is near death
q: Therefore he is near death.

s: Seers are wise (great, awakened, and free from acts)
q: Look! there are great Seers in the world, wise, awakened, free from acts.

s: Seers are awakened (great and free from acts)
q: Look! there are great Seers in the world, wise, awakened, free from acts.

s: Seers are free from acts (as great, wise, awakened beings)
q: Look! there are great Seers in the world, wise, awakened, free from acts.

s: Ginas declare truth (beyond doubt)
q: 'But that is truth beyond doubt, what has been declared by the Ginas.'

s: Self is knower (the experiencer)
q: The Self is the knower (or experiencer), and the knower is the Self.

s: knower is Self (the experiencer)
q: The Self is the knower (or experiencer), and the knower is the Self.

s: right doctrine of Self is maintained by he
q: Such is he who maintains the right doctrine of Self.

s: fool is far from final liberation
q: Because he is near death, he is far (from liberation).

s: Tîrthakaras provide teaching (through their teaching)
q: He who is great and withdraws his mind from the outer world, should learn the teaching (of the Tîrthakaras) through the teaching (of the âkârya);

s: the sacred lore enables victory for a hero (desiring liberation)
q: Desiring liberation, a hero should, through the sacred lore, ever be victorious.

s: currents of sin come from above (and from below and the sides)
q: The current (of sin) is said to come from above, from below, and from the sides; these have been declared to be the currents through which, look, there is sinfulness.

s: birth and death are left by liberated (after leaving the road to birth and death)
q: Knowing whence we come and whither we go, he leaves the road to birth and death, rejoicing in the glorious (liberation).

s: liberated is without the body (as an unconditioned being)
q: he is without body, without resurrection, without contact (of matter)

s: liberated perceives truth (as one who knows and sees)
q: such a great man, free from acts, knows and sees the truth;

s: liberated soul has no form (its essence is without form)
q: its essence is without form; there is no condition of the unconditioned.

s: liberated soul has no sound (nor colour, smell, taste, or touch)
q: There is no sound, no colour, no smell, no taste, no touch--nothing of that kind.

s: life resembles dewdrop (for a slow and ignorant fool)
q: considers the life of a slow and ignorant fool as similar to a dewdrop trembling on the sharp point of the blade of Kusa grass which falls down when shaken by the wind.

s: fool does injurious deeds (ignorantly)
q: A fool, doing cruel acts, comes thereby ignorantly to grief.
